handback.title: Work splits into stories by the files it changes
handback.summary: Each criterion lists the code files it changes, and code groups criteria into stories by shared files, with no caps.
handback.feature: Criteria list their files; code groups them into stories by shared files. Shared files take turns to build. Owner steps sit on the plan.

stories.title: Each criterion lists the code files it changes
stories.user_story: Every plan shows which code files each criterion changes, so code can split and fence by them.
stories.context: Today a plan has one scope list for the whole story (`scope` in plan.json, checked in `from_kind` in `dokima/planner.py`); criteria carry no files. Add a `files` list to every criterion, in user stories and in a split's stories (`check_stories`). A path that does not exist yet is fine: the worker creates it. The planner's instructions live in `dokima/roles/planner.md` and `dokima/roles/plan-grade.md`; this issue explicitly asks to change how the planner tags criteria, so those files are in reach. Tests sit beside `tests/test_plan_shape.py` and `tests/test_planner_prompt.py`.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each criterion in a plan carries a list of the code files it changes.
acceptance_criteria.words: Each criterion carries a `files` list in the plan's structured output: the code files it changes, at least one.

edge_cases.case: A files field that is text, not a list, is rejected naming the criterion.

acceptance_criteria.text: The plan check rejects a plan where any criterion lists no file, naming that criterion.
acceptance_criteria.words: Code rejects a plan where a criterion lists none.

acceptance_criteria.text: The plan check accepts a criterion listing a file that does not exist yet.
acceptance_criteria.words: A file it creates counts by its path.

edge_cases.case: A new file inside a folder that does not exist yet.

acceptance_criteria.text: The planner's instructions say a criterion lists every file its behavior needs, never just one.
acceptance_criteria.words: A criterion lists every file its behavior needs, never just one, so a behavior is never cut across stories.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: It is a rule the planner reads, with no input of its own.

acceptance_criteria.text: The planner's instructions say work that can be written as code is a criterion like any other.
acceptance_criteria.words: if it can be written as code (infrastructure as code, a setup script), it's a criterion like any other.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: It is a rule the planner reads, with no input of its own.

stories.title: A plan's scope comes from its criteria's files
stories.user_story: The worker may change exactly the files the criteria list, plus their tests, with no separate scope to keep.
stories.context: The fence (`dokima/fence.py`, `fence()`) reads the scope from plan.json's `scope` or the issue's Scope heading (`scope_of`). `dokima/planner.py` `plan_text` writes that heading. After this story the scope is the union of every criterion's `files` plus the tests the plan names; a plan still carrying `scope` is rejected, the way retired fields are (`problems_old` in `dokima/agent_checks.py`). Criteria already quote the owner's words, checked by `check_words` in `dokima/planner.py` and pinned by `tests/test_criteria_quote_owner.py`; keep that working.

acceptance_criteria.text: A plan's scope is every file its criteria list, plus the tests the plan names.
acceptance_criteria.words: The plan's scope is all criteria's files plus their tests

edge_cases.case: Two criteria listing the same file give it once in the scope.

acceptance_criteria.text: The plan check rejects a plan that still carries a separate scope field.
acceptance_criteria.words: with no separate scope field
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The field is either there or not; there is no other case.

acceptance_criteria.text: The fence undoes the worker's change to any file no criterion lists.
acceptance_criteria.words: The fence keeps enforcing it.

edge_cases.case: The worker creates a new file a criterion lists, and it is kept.

acceptance_criteria.text: The plan check rejects a criterion that does not quote the owner's own words.
acceptance_criteria.words: Each one quotes my words, which are the spec.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Already true today and pinned by an existing test; this story keeps it.

stories.title: Code groups criteria into stories by shared files
stories.user_story: Any ask, however big, splits into stories by the files its criteria change, never by counting.
stories.context: Today the planner picks stories itself and code only counts them: `check_size` and `PER_STORY = 5` in `dokima/planner.py`; the count rule is also written in `dokima/roles/planner.md` (Split) and `rules/splitting.md`. After this story the planner hands back criteria with files and code computes the groups: criteria sharing a code file, directly or through another criterion, are one story; each story is filed as a sub-issue by `file_split` in `dokima/agent_autopilot.py`. One group means one user story, no split. Files ending in .md are ignored when grouping.

acceptance_criteria.text: Code puts criteria that share any code file into the same story.
acceptance_criteria.words: Code groups criteria that share any code file into one story (a sub-issue).

edge_cases.case: A shares a file with B, and B with C: all three are one story.

acceptance_criteria.text: Criteria with no code file in common become separate stories.
acceptance_criteria.words: Criteria with no file in common become separate stories.

edge_cases.case: Every criterion shares one file, so the plan stays a single story.

acceptance_criteria.text: No count of criteria or stories splits or refuses a plan; today's count rules are gone.
acceptance_criteria.words: No number decides it: no criteria cap, no story cap.

edge_cases.case: A plan of twenty criteria sharing one file passes as one story.

acceptance_criteria.text: Two criteria that share only a markdown file stay in separate stories.
acceptance_criteria.words: Markdown files never group criteria
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The case is the criterion itself; normal use adds none.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each edge case stays under its criterion and never changes how criteria group.
acceptance_criteria.words: Edge cases stay under their criterion and don't affect the split.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The case is the criterion itself; normal use adds none.

stories.title: Stories sharing a code file take turns to build
stories.user_story: Two stories never build the same file at once, while planning and review go on freely.
stories.context: No build waits on another today. The worker is started from `dokima/agent_next.py` (`next_step`) and `dokima/agent_roles.py` (`start_waiting`); planner and plan-review starts must not be touched by the wait. The owner settled it: a story's turn ends when its pull request merges. Markdown files never cause a wait. Each story already merges to main on its own pull request with no parent branch; keep it so and pin it. A story's own planner may add files beyond the ones its split gave it; before the worker starts, the clash check runs again on the story's final file list.

acceptance_criteria.text: A story's build waits until another open story sharing a code file has its pull request merged.
acceptance_criteria.words: A story's turn ends when its PR merges.

edge_cases.case: The other story merges, and the waiting build starts.

acceptance_criteria.text: Planning and plan review of a story never wait on another story's files.
acceptance_criteria.words: Planning and plan review never wait; only the worker's build does.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The case is the criterion itself; normal use adds none.

acceptance_criteria.text: A shared markdown file never makes a story's build wait.
acceptance_criteria.words: Markdown files never group criteria and never make a story wait.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The case is the criterion itself; normal use adds none.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each story merges to main on its own pull request, with no parent branch.
acceptance_criteria.words: Stories merge to main one by one. No parent branch.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Already true today; this story pins it.

acceptance_criteria.text: A story whose plan adds files beyond those it was assigned is checked again for clashes before it builds.
acceptance_criteria.words: a story whose plan changes files beyond the ones it was assigned is checked again for clashes before it builds.

edge_cases.case: The added file is held by another open story, so the build waits.
The added file is held by no other story, so the build starts.

stories.title: Steps only the owner can do sit on the plan
stories.user_story: Interactive steps, like a console or a secret, show on the plan as the owner's, blocking only what needs them.
stories.context: Today a plan has no place for a step that changes no file. The issue says nothing waits on such a step by itself; the newer comment adds that stories building on it are blocked until the owner closes it. Both hold: only the stories that build on it wait. The plan reads 'close it' as the step being its own issue the owner closes, linked as blocked-by the way `file_split` in `dokima/agent_autopilot.py` links stories.

acceptance_criteria.text: A step that changes no file is listed on the plan as the owner's to do.
acceptance_criteria.words: it's a step for me on the plan
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The case is the criterion itself; normal use adds none.

acceptance_criteria.text: Stories that build on an owner's step stay blocked until the owner closes it.
acceptance_criteria.words: the stories that build on it are blocked by it until I close it.

edge_cases.case: The owner closes the step, and the blocked story starts.

acceptance_criteria.text: Stories that do not build on an owner's step never wait on it.
acceptance_criteria.words: Nothing waits on it by itself.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: The case is the criterion itself; normal use adds none.

stories.title: Red first stays and unproven criteria show on the card
stories.user_story: Every criterion is proven red first, and the card shows which criteria are not verified.
stories.context: Red first already holds: `passing_today` in `dokima/planner.py` rejects a new test that passes on main. The planner's instructions already say an ask that cannot be tested becomes a question. The card (`dokima/card.py`, which this issue explicitly asks to change) shows no 'not verified' today for a (manual) criterion. The owner dropped naming a crowded file on the card.

acceptance_criteria.words: Red first stays: every criterion's test fails on main before work starts.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: Already true today and pinned by an existing test; this story keeps it.
